doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: LA club scene and movie star bands
summary: Clubs he works now, Jeff Goldblum, Peter Weller and George Segal.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Is the live jazz scene healthy around here or not?

Yeah it always has been for me. I always work good and there’s a place called Steamers, a great club in Fullerton wherever that is, somewhere way out somewhere. I worked there. We’re going to record there in April. And I work at Chadney’s every Sunday night with Ross Tompkins, we do a duet. And then I work with the big band and work different

places with the quartet: Spagitinni’s and different clubs, the Catalinas in Hollywood, and I work sometimes with Jeff Goldblum, with a movie star band, with Peter Weller plays trumpet and Jeff Goldblum plays piano.
And when we work a place you can’t get in to that place.
Yeah he’s pretty good, for a movie star.
He’s good for a movie star.
They got their own way of playing, movie stars. You play a little, you pose a little. I worked a lot with George Segal.
George Segal, heck of a banjo player, isn’t he?
He plays good, yeah. And he promised me he’s going to learn another chord next year.
Maybe even a minor one, huh?
I doubt that, I don’t want to hope for too much. But he’s a good actor though, and he acts like he’s playing.
